title: Higher Ed Produces Uniquely Ethical Leadership
author: Patrick Dempsey
summary: Patrick Dempsey responds to a common rebuttal against AI's disruption of higher education -- that universities develop ethical, civic-minded actors capable of moral reasoning -- by producing a list of high-profile corporate fraudsters whose credentials span the most prestigious institutions in the world. The list includes Enron's Jeffrey Skilling (Harvard MBA), Theranos's Elizabeth Holmes (Stanford), FTX's Sam Bankman-Fried (MIT), and Bernie Madoff (Hofstra), among many others. Dempsey notes the list is not politically curated and makes only two observations at the end: Harvard appears eight times, Wharton four times, Princeton twice, and NYU twice. The article's implied argument is that credential prestige does not predict ethical leadership, undermining the claim that higher education's irreducible value lies in moral formation.
points: The most common institutional rebuttal to AI's disruption of higher education -- that universities develop ethical actors and civic-minded citizens -- is refuted empirically by the credential profiles of the most consequential corporate fraudsters in modern American history.

Jeffrey Skilling (Harvard MBA, top 5%), Andrew Fastow (Northwestern/Kellogg MBA), Ken Lay (Missouri/Houston PhD), and Bernie Madoff (Hofstra) represent Enron alone -- one company, four credentialed fraudsters.

Sam Bankman-Fried (MIT, BS physics) was raised on the Stanford campus by two law professors and still oversaw the theft of billions in customer funds -- a direct counter-example to the 'ethical formation' thesis.
Harvard appears 8 times in the full list, Wharton 4 times, Princeton and NYU twice each -- the institutions most associated with elite moral formation account for more than half the entries.

Dempsey offers no argument beyond the list itself: the data is the point, and the point is that the 'irreducible value' claim -- the one thing higher education insists AI cannot replicate -- does not survive contact with the credential records of those who did the most institutional damage.
quotes: AI is dismantling the traditional value proposition of higher education. It is collapsing the institution's role as gatekeeper of information, displacing its function as transmitter of knowledge, and putting direct pressure on its claim as validator of competency.

The most common rebuttal is this: higher education develops the person. It produces ethical actors. It forms civic-minded citizens capable of moral reasoning. That is the irreducible value. That's the thing AI -- and apparently nothing else -- cannot replicate.

Jeffrey Skilling earned his MBA from Harvard Business School, graduating in the top five percent of his class. As CEO of Enron, he oversaw one of the largest corporate frauds in American history, wiping out the retirement savings of thousands of employees and triggering the largest bankruptcy in U.S. history at the time.
